currentContext.business: SML supplies medium and heavy-duty cranes on a rental basis to private and public sector undertakings and delivers integrated lifting and project execution services, enabled by in-house engineering and project planning. The Group operates through three stated verticals: Crane Rental and Heavy Lift Solutions (the core vertical), Turnkey Solutions in Wind EPC (through Sangreen Future Renewables Private Limited), and Logistics for Cranes and Heavy Machinery (through Sangreen Logistics Private Limited), serving sectors such as renewables, logistics and core industries. It has moved from crane rental towards an integrated 'concept-to-commissioning' approach in wind energy, and has extended operations to Saudi Arabia and Botswana.

currentContext.expansion: FY2025-26 was a fleet- and geography-expansion year executed under the Elevate 2030 roadmap. The Corporate Overview 'New Developments' spread states the Company 'Revised 2025-26 CAPEX to Rs 639 crore', with Rs 415 crore allocated to India and Rs 224 crore allocated to Saudi Arabia, and focussed investments in high-capacity cranes (350 MT / 320 MT) to address demand in renewables and infrastructure. The MD&A separately states a total capital expenditure of Rs 474 crore incurred during 2025-26, comprising Rs 373 crore in India and Rs 101 crore in the Saudi Arabian subsidiary, with Rs 165 crore deferred to 2026-27; the MD&A also states the Rs 474 crore was invested 'in capability expansion, including the addition of 132 new cranes taking cumulative lifting capacity to 22,450 MTPA', and that a monetisation of 132 cranes took place during the year (the profit figure on that monetisation is a P&L item and is deliberately not reproduced). The two capex framings are recorded exactly as printed and are not reconciled - see notes. Geographic expansion: Saudi Arabia was operationalised through Sanghvi Movers Middle East, achieving go-to-market status with commercial operations commencing in September, over 30 cranes deployed directly from port to site at 100% utilisation, and 36 cranes added in the Saudi operation during FY2025-26 against capital expenditure of Rs 101 crore there; the MD has committed approximately Rs 225 crore towards scaling the Saudi fleet to upwards of 100 machines over the next 24 months, with an ambition of a top-tier position over five years and Saudi Arabia established as the operating hub with a pathway to GCC leadership. Africa entry was made through the first heavy-lift order in Botswana (Sanghvi Movers Botswana Proprietary Limited, Gaborone), and initial inquiries were received from Qatar (step-down subsidiary Sanghvi Movers Middle East Qatar Limited). Structurally, the renewables business was carved out into Sangreen Future Renewables Private Limited, and Sangreen Logistics Private Limited was set up for crane and heavy-machinery logistics. The Elevate 2030 'Financial Direction' anchors capital deployment of approximately Rs 500 crore alongside a revenue scale-up to Rs 1,800 crore by 2027-28, and the roadmap's 'Operating Scale' focus area commits to expanding the depot footprint and standardising the operating model. The physical footprint stated is 15 Company-owned depots across 12 states (BRSR states 15 states and 19 national offices, 0 plants), 175 acres of freehold land for crane parking, 4 regional offices and the registered office at Tathawade, Pune, with cranes operating at more than 130 customer locations across India as of March 31, 2026. Fleet is stated at 550+ cranes and 200+ specialised transport equipment (BRSR states 'over 450 cranes' with lifting capacities from 40 MT to 1600 MT); 1,600 MT crawler cranes were procured in 2024 and one was used for the largest ROB girder launch in the Company's history (700 MT over a 72 m span at Nagpur). An MoU was signed with Action Construction Equipment Limited (ACE) for deployment of indigenously manufactured heavy cranes in India.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity in the domestic crane rental market
risks.note: Explicitly listed under MD&A THREATS: 'Heightened competitive intensity in the domestic crane rental market, which may exert pressure on yields and margins despite sustained demand.' This bears directly on the two KPIs management runs the business on - average blended yield (2.12% per month) and fleet utilisation - and the MD&A concedes the Company relied on 'value-led customer engagement, disciplined asset deployment and calibrated commercial interventions to sustain yields and margins'.

MD&A THREATS: 'Reliance on specialised equipment imported from Germany and China exposes the Company to procurement delays, logistics risks, and potential changes in customs duties.' For an asset-heavy rental model where growth is delivered by adding high-capacity cranes, procurement lead-time or duty changes directly gate the capex programme; the MoU with Action Construction Equipment Limited for indigenously manufactured heavy cranes is the stated structural response.

risks.risk: Execution and external delays causing order-book slippage
risks.note: MD&A THREATS: 'Delays in project execution due to seasonal factors or customer site readiness may result in 10-15% of the order book carrying over into the next financial period.' This is a quantified, recurring revenue-recognition risk on a business whose visibility case rests on the order book, and it sits alongside the Rs 165 crore of FY2025-26 capex that was itself deferred to 2026-27.

risks.risk: Revenue volatility in the EPC businesses under percentage-of-completion
risks.note: MD&A THREATS and segment commentary: revenue can fluctuate in the EPC businesses because of the percentage-of-completion method, 'especially in the early stages of a project'. As the Wind EPC and Project EPC verticals are the stated diversification engines and are scaling from a low base, reported performance may vary between periods independent of underlying demand; the Company states it selects contracts on execution capability and profitability thresholds.

risks.risk: Cost structure and localisation burden in new international geographies
risks.note: MD&A THREATS: 'Higher operating costs in international markets such as Saudi Arabia, driven by manpower requirements, regulatory compliance, and localisation norms, impacting overall cost structures.' The segment commentary confirms that higher manpower, logistics and maintenance costs partly offset the superior Saudi yield advantage, with the Saudi business only beginning to generate positive monthly EBITDA - so the growth engine carries a margin-dilution risk while it scales.

A structural concentration disclosed without being labelled a risk: BRSR Section A states crane hiring services account for 93.36% of turnover (Project EPC 6.63%), exports are 0% of turnover, and international markets served are stated as 0 countries. Notwithstanding the Saudi Arabia, Botswana and Qatar entities, the disclosed revenue base is overwhelmingly one activity in one country, so a domestic capex-cycle downturn or a single-sector demand shock transmits with little offset. (BRSR item 23 and the concentration items are read from the routed BRSR pages in this bundle.)

risks.risk: Workforce attrition and occupational health & safety exposure
risks.note: BRSR turnover rates jumped to 42.47% for permanent employees (18.22%/30.77%/19.06% split the prior year) and 77.00% for permanent workers (2.52% prior year) in FY2025-26 - the Company attributes this to Elevate 2030 growth and expansion. Separately, BRSR material issue 7 'Operational Health & Safety' flags accident, injury and fatality risk, 'especially among temporary workers who may lack sufficient training or experience', with serious incidents capable of causing project delays and downtime. For a business whose moat is stated to be execution and safety, a >40% attrition rate is a structural capability risk.

PROVENANCE: back-filled from the SIBLING capex_expansion bundle (Independent Auditor's Report CARO annexure, which arrived there mis-headed as BRSR); no litigation section was routed into this risks bundle. Disputed statutory dues on crane hiring remain unpaid under the Central Sales Tax Act 1956 (FY2010-11 to FY2017-18), Gujarat VAT 2003 (FY2008-09), Maharashtra VAT 2002 (FY2010-11 to FY2017-18) and multiple GST matters across Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha (FY2018-19 to FY2025-26), pending before the Bombay High Court, state sales tax tribunals, Joint/Additional Commissioners and GST appellate authorities. The auditor also reports provident-fund dues for May-August 2025 outstanding beyond six months and 'Not paid till date' as at March 31, 2026. Amounts deliberately not reproduced.

one-line thesis: Sanghvi Movers delivered strong FY26 growth (37% revenue, 16% EBITDA) driven by 35% core rental growth and a doubling of its asset-light renewables EPC book, though blended margins compressed due to the mix shift. The strategic pivot to KSA is nearing cumulative profitability with high yields (4.5%), while a record INR 4,000 crore inquiry pipeline supports a guided 30% consolidated growth trajectory for FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,070cr (+37% YoY); EBITDA: INR 429cr (+16% YoY), Margin 40.1% (-290bps YoY due to low-margin EPC mix); PAT: INR 184cr (+18% YoY); Order Book: INR 1,053cr (100% executable in FY27); Net Debt: INR 612cr (0.47x D/E). One-offs: No major one-offs in Q4, but FY26 PAT comparison noted an exceptional item in Q3 FY26; Accounting distortion: Blended margin decline masks stable/high margins in core rental (40%+) vs low-margin/high-ROCE EPC.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~30% consolidated for FY27; Margin: No blended target (BU-level P&L), Core Rental ~40-45%, KSA targeting 45-48%; Order Inflow: INR 4,000cr inquiry pipeline; Capex: INR 390cr (India) + INR 200cr (KSA) planned for FY27.
order book & pipeline: INR 1,053 crores as of May 14, 2026; 100% executable within FY27; Inquiry pipeline stands at INR 4,000 crores.
segment / subsidiary detail: Crane Rental (65% of FY26 rev): +35% growth, 79% utilization, 2.12% blended yield (India 2.24% in Q4, KSA >4.5%). Renewables EPC (31% of FY26 rev): Revenue doubled YoY, asset-light, high ROCE (~70%), lower EBITDA margin. Project EPC (4%): Minor contribution.
growth verticals / optionality: KSA expansion (INR 50mn pipeline next 24mo); Nuclear sector push (govt mission); Wind capacity target (100GW by 2030); Refinery & Steel capex cycles.
margins & cost dynamics: Diesel cost impact mitigated: 50% contracts have free fuel supply, 50% under price revision discussion. Employee costs up 103% YoY due to EPC scale-up and leadership hiring. KSA operating costs higher but yields (4.5%) offset this, targeting 45-48% EBITDA.
capex / expansion: FY26 Actual: INR 474cr (India 373cr, KSA 101cr). FY27 Planned: INR 390cr (India) + INR 200cr (KSA). Deferred FY26 capex of INR 123cr (57 cranes) moved to FY27 due to OEM/shipping delays.
capital allocation: Focus on fleet expansion (core rental) and KSA market penetration. Maintaining D/E below 0.5x despite capex. No dividend specifics mentioned, reinvestment prioritized for ELEVATE 2030 plan.
risks & watch-items: Supply chain disruptions (shipping congestion/costs to KSA); Execution delays in EPC due to POCM timing; Geopolitical tension in West Asia; Diesel price volatility; Margin dilution from EPC mix.
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on expansion (doubling down on KSA despite geopolitics); Transparent on margin mix shifts; Disciplined on EPC contract selection to protect ROCE.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'margin decline' is a mathematical artifact of adding a high-ROCE, low-margin EPC business to a high-margin rental book, not a deterioration in core operating efficiency. KSA business is already monthly EBITDA positive, faster than expected.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).
